system:
You are working for a client on a new software service. Nobody has designed it yet.

The client writes:

> Our customer companies need a new service for running their drone fleets from day to day, on our platform. Write the requirements for it: what the service must do, so that a team can build it and anyone can check whether it does.

What you know about the client's business:

A platform company runs a shared service for several independent drone operating companies. Its customers today include a parcel delivery firm, an infrastructure inspection firm, and a regional hospital logistics firm. Others are expected to join.

The customer companies compete with each other or work for clients who do. Each company's fleet, jobs, sites, and problems are its own business. They accept sharing airspace information, because that information comes from the authorities and is the same for everyone.

The people who will use the service work in three roles: fleet technician, dispatcher, airspace desk. You can reach one person in each role. A message that is exactly one line, `ASK <role>: <question>`, with `<role>` one of `technician`, `dispatcher` or `desk`, goes to that person, and their answer comes back to you. Each of them remembers what you asked them before. You can send at most 90 such questions in all. Any other message is taken as your requirements, and ends the work.

Write the requirements as a list in YAML, in exactly this format, with nothing else in that message:

```yaml
- id: DR-01
  requirement: >
    one thing the service must do, or must not do, and in which case
- id: DR-02
  requirement: >
    ...
```

Number the items DR-01, DR-02, and so on. Each item states one requirement in plain words.

messages.content: Begin.

content.text: ASK dispatcher: Please walk me through a typical working day: what do you do, step by step, to get a drone job planned, assigned, flown and closed, and what information do you need at each step?

messages.content: I plan and run the flights as a dispatcher, which includes deciding which drone flies and along which way, and I sign off a flight before it leaves. Several dispatchers plan at the same time, often for the same busy sites and popular drones, and our policy is that software never chooses a drone or a way for us. I do want help finding out which of my drones could get to where a job starts. Before and during a flight, outside people and devices report whether the load is ready, if the drone reaches its job points, and when it arrives.

content.text: ASK dispatcher: When several dispatchers plan at once for the same drone or the same busy site, what goes wrong today, and what should the service do when two plans want the same drone or the same site slot at the same time?

messages.content: I don't know.

content.text: ASK dispatcher: Can one drone be planned for two flights whose times overlap, and can a site (launch or landing place) take more than one drone at the same time? What are the limits?

messages.content: Sites have only so many places where drones can take off and land at the same time. My notes do not state whether one drone can be planned for two flights whose times overlap, so I don't know.

content.text: ASK dispatcher: When a site's take-off and landing places are all taken for the time you want, what should happen to your plan: refused, warned, or something else? And who sets the number of places a site has?

messages.content: I don't know what should happen to my plan, and I don't know who sets the number of places a site has.

content.text: ASK dispatcher: What do you check before you sign off a flight for departure, and what must be true for you to be allowed to sign it off?

messages.content: I am the licensed person responsible for each flight, and I decide which drone flies and along which way before signing off a flight before it leaves. I can call off a flight. My notes do not state what I check before I sign off a flight for departure or what must be true for me to be allowed to sign it off.

content.text: ASK dispatcher: You said you want help finding which of your drones could get to where a job starts. What makes a drone able or unable to get there (location, battery, range, load capacity, condition, airspace), and what should the service show you?

messages.content: Drones are of several models from different manufacturers that differ in how much they can carry, how far they can fly on a full battery, which sensors they carry, and which charging connector they use. Each drone has a home site, and batteries drain faster in cold and wind than planned. I don't know what the service should show me.

content.text: ASK dispatcher: The outside people and devices that report load readiness, job points reached, and arrival: who or what are they, how do their reports reach you, and what problems do you have with those reports (late, missing, duplicated, wrong order, from the wrong sender)?

messages.content: Reports come through relay stations because radio coverage is patchy, especially around ports, industrial sites, and in bad weather. Because of this, reports from drones can arrive late, out of order, more than once, or not at all. My notes do not state who or what the outside people and devices are.

content.text: ASK dispatcher: When reports arrive late, out of order, or twice, what do you need the service to do so that you still see the true state of a flight? And what should happen when no report arrives at all for a flight in the air?

messages.content: I don't know what I need the service to do when reports arrive late, out of order, or twice. My notes do not state what should happen when no report arrives at all for a flight in the air.

content.text: ASK dispatcher: What are all the things that can force you to change or call off a flight after you have planned it or signed it off, and what do you do in each case?

messages.content: I can call off a flight, and a closure can come into force while drones of several companies are already in the air. The authorities define zones where flying is prohibited and announce planned and sudden closures, which are often amended during the day. My notes do not state all the things that can force me to change a flight or what I do in each case.

content.text: ASK dispatcher: What does a job consist of (start point, job points, load, time window, needed sensors, client), where do jobs come from, and are there differences between the kinds of work (parcel delivery, inspection, hospital logistics) that the service must handle?

messages.content: Deliveries carry a load from one site to another, and inspections take a drone with the right sensors to a list of points in a set order and bring it back to where the inspection started. Drones fly along corridors between named sites. My notes do not state where jobs come from or what differences exist between the kinds of work the service must handle.

content.text: ASK technician: Please walk me through your typical working day: what do you do with the drones, step by step, what do you record, and what do you need from the new service?

messages.content: I keep the drones and charging equipment in working order, which involves adding new drones to the fleet, retiring old ones, setting up charging pads at our sites, taking drones out of service for repairs and putting them back, and sending drones to charge. Regulators can ask us to show how our drones have been looked after, and our repairs and servicing are carried out by technicians. I do not know anything about software or what is needed from the new service.

content.text: ASK technician: When you take a drone out of service for repair, what should happen to flights already planned for that drone, and to a flight it is flying right now? And who is allowed to put it back into service, under what conditions?

messages.content: I do not know how flights already planned or currently in flight are handled when I take a drone out of service. My notes state that I take drones out of service for repairs and put them back, and that repairs and servicing are carried out by technicians. However, my notes do not state any specific conditions for putting a drone back into service.

content.text: ASK technician: Tell me about charging: how do you send a drone to charge, what are the limits of charging pads (how many drones at once, which connectors, which sites), and what goes wrong with charging today?

messages.content: I send drones to charge, and we have a few dozen charging pads at our own sites. Several connector types are in use, and they are not interchangeable, while our pads are never lent to another company. What goes wrong today is that the links used to give instructions to the charging equipment are unreliable, meaning an instruction may get through twice and the sender often cannot tell whether the first attempt arrived.

content.text: ASK technician: When an instruction to the charging equipment gets through twice, or you cannot tell if it arrived, what harm does it cause, and how do you find out what the pad is really doing?

messages.content: I do not know what harm a duplicated or unconfirmed instruction causes. My notes do not say how I find out what the charging pad is really doing.

content.text: ASK technician: What records must you be able to show regulators about how drones have been looked after, how far back, and are there rules about changing or deleting those records?

messages.content: Regulators can ask us to show how our drones have been looked after, and our repairs and servicing are carried out by technicians. My notes do not state how far back these records must go. My notes also state that none of the companies is seeking certification from the platform, and that there are no data-retention or deletion features.

content.text: ASK technician: Are the technicians who repair and service your drones all your own company's staff, or do some outside or contract technicians (perhaps working for several companies) do this work? What may each see and do?

messages.content: I do not know whether the technicians who repair and service our drones are our own staff or outside contractors. My notes state that repairs and servicing are carried out by technicians, and that each company's fleet, jobs, sites, and problems are its own business.

content.text: ASK technician: When you add a new drone to the fleet or retire one, what details do you record about it, and what should happen to a retired drone's history and to anything still planned for it?

messages.content: I add new drones to the fleet and retire old ones, but my notes do not state what details I record about them. My notes also do not say what should happen to a retired drone's history or to anything still planned for it.

content.text: ASK technician: Besides repairs, what else do you know about drones that dispatchers need to know before using one (battery level, faults, servicing due, where it is)? And what problems do you have today working with dispatchers?

messages.content: I do not know what else dispatchers need to know before using a drone, or what problems I have working with them. My notes state that I keep drones and charging equipment in working order, add new drones to the fleet, retire old ones, set up charging pads at our sites, take drones out of service for repairs and put them back, and send drones to charge.

content.text: ASK desk: Please walk me through your typical working day: what do you do, step by step, with airspace information, who do you work for, and what do you need from the new service?

messages.content: I work for the airspace desk at the platform company, keeping the shared picture of the airspace that includes the network of flight corridors between sites, the zones grouping them, and closures announced by the authorities. I enter closures and want to know how much disruption a closure caused across customers. The authorities define zones where flying is prohibited and announce planned and sudden closures, which are often amended during the day.

content.text: ASK desk: When you want to know how much disruption a closure caused across customers, what exactly do you want to see, and how much of each customer company's flights, drones and jobs are you allowed to see?

messages.content: I don't know. Each company's fleet, jobs, sites, and problems are its own business, and I have no business looking into any one company's operations.

content.text: ASK desk: What exactly does a closure cover (a zone, single corridors, sites?), what times does it have, and when the authorities amend a closure during the day, what can change (start, end, area, cancelled altogether) and how should the service treat the earlier version?

messages.content: I don't know.

content.text: ASK desk: When you enter a closure that takes effect while drones of several companies are already in the air in the affected area, what must happen: who must be told, how fast, and what must they be told?

messages.content: I don't know.

content.text: ASK desk: What is the relation between zones, corridors and sites in the picture you keep? Who may add or change corridors and zones, and how often does that happen?

messages.content: I don't know.
